What I ran, on Windows with Python 3.13 against crewAI main (40bb2d3) and this PR head (255ee13):

- The new test `TestNativeProviderAfterHooksAsync::test_global_after_hook_runs_on_direct_acall` fails on main at the `acall` assertion (the response stays `the SECRET is 42`) and passes on the PR. `llm.call()` already redacted on main, so the gap is real.
- `lib/crewai/tests/hooks/test_llm_hooks.py` passes on the PR (28 passed).
- I wrote one extra throwaway probe for the OpenAI chat-completions async streaming path (`_ahandle_streaming_completion`), using real `ChatCompletionChunk` objects, `stream=True` and a global after hook that replaces SECRET. On main `acall` returns `the SECRET is 42` and `call` returns `the [REDACTED] is 42`. On the PR both return `the [REDACTED] is 42`.
- I ran `lib/crewai/tests/hooks` and `lib/crewai/tests/llms/hooks` on both trees. Both give 25 failures on main and on the PR; the PR has one more pass than main (the new test). I did not look into why those 25 fail, and I did not run the failing ones in isolation.

What I only read, did not run: the Anthropic async paths (`_ahandle_completion`, `_ahandle_streaming_completion`), the Bedrock paths (`_handle_streaming_converse`, `_ahandle_converse`) and the OpenAI Responses async paths. The Anthropic and Bedrock SDKs are not installed in my venv. In each of these the new call sits in the same place relative to `_emit_call_completed_event` as the existing sync hook call, and `_invoke_after_llm_call_hooks` returns early for non-str responses and when `model_call_hooks_already_dispatched()` is true, so I do not expect double dispatch under the executor. That second part is from reading `base_llm.py`, not from a run.

One thing to check by the author: the `_handle_streaming_converse` hunk in `bedrock/completion.py` is the sync streaming path, not an async one. It looks correct to me, but the PR title and description talk about async only, so it may be worth a line in the description and a test.

I found no bug in the parts I ran.

Provider/path audit: this is broader than the three direct native providers, but not every provider needs a local edit.

| Route | Async non-streaming | Async streaming | Required action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI Chat Completions | missing before this PR | already dispatched in `_finalize_streaming_response` | add non-streaming only; retain exactly one streaming dispatch |
| OpenAI Responses | missing | missing | this PR correctly adds both |
| Anthropic | missing | missing | this PR correctly adds both |
| Bedrock Converse | missing | already present | add non-streaming; sync streaming also needed |
| Azure AI Inference / Gemini | present | present | no direct provider change |
| Azure Responses | inherits OpenAI Responses | inherits OpenAI Responses | covered transitively by the OpenAI fix |
| OpenAI-compatible providers and Snowflake | inherit OpenAI Chat behavior | inherit OpenAI Chat behavior | covered transitively, but must retain exactly one streaming dispatch |
| Generic LiteLLM-backed `LLM` route | missing | missing | still unaddressed |

One blocker in the current OpenAI diff: `_ahandle_streaming_completion` now calls `_invoke_after_llm_call_hooks(...) ` after `_finalize_streaming_response(...) `, but that shared finalizer already invokes the hook for string responses. The new wrapper will therefore run streaming hooks twice (non-idempotent hooks can rewrite/abort twice). Please remove the outer async-stream wrapper, or move the single dispatch to one canonical layer.

Separately, the generic LiteLLM-backed `LLM.acall()` path has no after-hook invocation at all; I reproduced it with a mocked raw response. It needs the same parity treatment (and regression coverage) if this PR intends to make direct `acall()` behavior consistently match `call()` across providers.

Correction to my prior review after checking the PR base commit: `OpenAICompletion._finalize_streaming_response` returns raw text, so the new async-stream wrapper is **not** a double dispatch.

The remaining gap is the synchronous OpenAI Chat Completions streaming route: it also calls that finalizer but never invokes `after_llm_call`. The best placement is a single string-result dispatch in `_finalize_streaming_response`, then remove the async-only wrapper. That gives both sync and async streaming exactly one invocation and also covers OpenAI-compatible providers and Snowflake through inheritance.

Revised coverage table:

| Route | Status after this PR | Where it should be handled |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI Chat Completions — sync streaming | **Still missing** | `OpenAICompletion._finalize_streaming_response` once per string result |
| OpenAI Chat Completions — async streaming | Covered by this PR | Prefer the shared finalizer above |
| Generic LiteLLM `LLM.acall()` — non-streaming | **Still missing** | Wrap a string result in `LLM.acall()`, mirroring `LLM.call()` |
| Generic LiteLLM `LLM.acall()` — streaming | **Still missing** | Same common wrapper |
| OpenAI Responses, native Anthropic, native Bedrock | Covered by this PR | — |
| Azure and Gemini | Already covered | — |
| Azure Responses API | Covered through its OpenAI delegate | — |
| OpenAI-compatible providers and Snowflake | Inherit the OpenAI streaming gap | Covered by the shared finalizer |

I also reproduced the generic LiteLLM async bypass with a mocked response. Please add regression coverage for the shared OpenAI streaming path and generic `LLM.acall()`; the existing direct OpenAI non-streaming test does not exercise either.

### Recursive converse wraps HookAborted **Medium Severity** Moving after-hooks outside the converse `try` only protects the leaf text path. Native tool execution still `return`s into a recursive converse from inside that `try`, so a `HookAborted` from the follow-up hooks is caught by `except Exception` and re-raised as `RuntimeError`. Direct `call()`/`acall()` with `available_functions` therefore still lose the abort.

**Preserve hook aborts after recursive tool calls.**

If `available_functions` executes a tool, the handler returns a recursive Converse call from inside its outer `try`.
